anchors.prompt: Same kitchen as the input photo, but now he stands at the gas stove on the right side of the kitchen, the camera turned a little to the right: on the front burner a small steel pot with a little water, inside it an open glass jar of pale golden oil with dried culinary bay leaves (Laurus nobilis: dry, matte olive-green, elongated oval leaves with slightly wavy edges, like the ones from a supermarket spice bag; only dry leaves, no flowers anywhere); on the counter beside the stove: a folded white kitchen towel with a clean empty glass jar upside down drying on it, and a second glass jar of CLOUDY oil with little white specks floating in it. The book and the aloe are gone. Waist-up, about two meters, the stove and that counter corner in frame, room around him. He rests one hand on the counter, looking at the viewer.

Same place, same framing and same light: the cloudy jar stands pushed to the side of the counter; he holds his thumb and index finger together as if showing a drop of water, eyebrows raised.

clips.text: A ver, vamos con calma, porque aquí es donde se equivoca casi todo el mundo. Y te lo cuento con un caso real.
clips.action: Leaning with one hand on the counter beside the stove, he talks calmly, then points down at the pot with the jar of oil.

clips.text: Doña Elena, setenta y tres años. Hizo su aceite, contentísima, y a las dos semanas me trae el frasco. Turbio. Con unos puntitos blancos flotando.
clips.action: He picks up the glass jar of cloudy oil from the counter and holds it toward the camera, turning it slowly so the little white specks floating inside are visible.

clips.text: Moho. ¿Y sabes por qué? Porque lavó las hojas y las metió mojadas al frasco. Y un aceite con agua adentro... se echa a perder.
clips.action: He shakes the spoiled jar a little, sets it down far to the side with a disapproving face, and makes a 'water dripping' gesture with his fingers.

clips.text: Una gota de agua basta. Por eso: hojas secas, frasco seco, cuchara seca. Si lavas el frasco, lo dejas secar un día entero boca abajo.
clips.action: EXTREME CLOSE-UP of the HANDS ONLY: his hand lifts the upside-down clean glass jar from the towel, turns it upright and wipes the inside with a dry cotton cloth.

clips.text: Ese es el error número uno. Y hay un segundo, casi igual de común: el calor. La gente pone el frasco directo al fuego, o hierve el agua fuerte.
clips.action: He sets the jar down, holds up one finger, then two fingers, and gestures at the burner flame with a worried face.

clips.text: Y el aceite se recalienta, huele a quemado, y en vez de cuidar la piel, la irrita. Por eso te digo: fuego mínimo, el agua apenas temblando.
clips.action: He mimes sniffing a burnt smell with a grimace, then lowers his flat hand slowly to show a very low flame, and nods.

clips.text: Mira, así. Burbujitas chiquitas en el fondo, nada más. Si metes el dedo en el agua, está caliente, pero se aguanta.
clips.action: EXTREME CLOSE-UP, no hands: tiny bubbles form on the bottom of the pot and rise slowly around the glass jar, faint steam, the golden oil still.

clips.text: Yo le pongo un trapito doblado en el fondo de la olla, para que el vidrio no toque directo el metal. Truco de abuela, eh.
clips.action: He lifts the jar a little with a folded cloth, shows the folded rag lying on the bottom of the pot under it, and puts the jar back.

clips.text: Treinta, cuarenta minutos. Si tienes paciencia, una hora, con el fuego al mínimo mínimo. Más tiempo no le hace daño. Más calor, sí.
clips.action: He looks at his black smartwatch, taps it, then makes a patient, calming gesture with both hands.

clips.text: Y mientras tanto, la cocina huele a laurel. A mí me recuerda a la cocina de mi mamá, los domingos, con la olla del caldo.
clips.action: He leans over the pot, closes his eyes and breathes in the aroma with a nostalgic smile, then looks back at the viewer.

clips.text: Cuando termina, apagas, y lo dejas enfriar dentro del agua, despacito. Nunca lo pases de golpe a algo frío, que el vidrio se puede romper.
clips.action: EXTREME CLOSE-UP of the HAND ONLY: his hand turns the black knob of the gas stove to off and the small blue flame disappears; the jar stays in the warm water.

clips.text: Y después, tapado, reposa hasta el otro día. Las hojas siguen soltando lo suyo mientras se enfría. No lo apures.
clips.action: He places the metal lid loosely on the jar, pats the lid, and raises a calm palm meaning 'wait'.

clips.text: Ahora, antes de ponértelo en la cara, hay una cosa que no te puedes saltar. Ninguna. Vamos a la mesa.
clips.action: He dries his hands on the kitchen towel, raises a finger, then gestures toward the left of the frame and starts to walk that way.
